#5255. Is poor demand the reason behind Roundhill ditching XRP, Solana income ETF plans?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

On the back of an iffy Q3, many were hoping Q4 would turn out to be better. Unfortunately, that hasn’t been the case. Especially for those in the XRP and Solana markets.

Both these altcoins are in the news today after Roundhill ETF Trust revealed that it will be ditching plans to launch two exchange-traded funds or ETFs tied to them. It cited no specific reason in its filings with the U.S Securities and Exchange Commission for these new plans.

The Trust no longer intends to seek effectiveness of the Fund.

It went on to add that “… no securities of the Fund were sold, or will be sold.”

The registration documents for both these ETFs were filed way back in October 2025. That’s over a year ago. As recently as 06 November, the Trust had submitted an extension. This would have allowed the registrations to become effective by 06 December.

However, an important distinction must be made here. It must be pointed out that the ETFs Roundhill was planning to launch were income-focused products. These ETFs would have relied on income generated by trading Options linked to existing crypto prodcuts.

Now, while more recent and fewer in number compared to funds that directly hold these tokens, these products have seen little interest lately.

Consider Amplify’s SOLM, for instance. At the time of writing, it held net assets worth just $1.36 million. This, despite being launched in November last year. Similarly, the fund manager’s XRPM had net assets worth just over $7.66 million in over a year since its launch.

These numbers are pretty startling, especially when compared to and juxtaposed against the figures reported by other Solana or XRP-focused ETFs. According to SoSoValue, for instance, combined, both these ETF products attracted over $969 million from May to October 2026.

This, despite recent market weakness hitting these ETF products too. Less than 24 hours ago, XRP ETFs saw outflows of over $6 million, with the Canary XRP ETF (XRPC) and the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF (GXRP) particulalry affected. This, after the week ending ending 13th November saw outflows of $19.1 million. This was the largest single-week withdrawal in nearly eight months.

In a similar vein, the assets under management for Spot Solana ETFs fell from $1.79 billion on 25th September to $947 million on 18th November.

#5253. How to Lose Your Love Handles

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

WHEN YOU THINK about a lover’s touch, your brain might jump to a pair of hands lingering around the hips—which might explain the origin of the term "love handles." It’s a cute nickname, but you’d probably describe love handles themselves as anything but cute.

The term refers to the pesky fat that sits on top of your hip bones, and lots of guys want it gone. “Many men are concerned about how to lose weight in their midsection. I let them know that their body has an android distribution, or male-like, weight distribution,” says Fatima Cody Stanford, M.D., M.P.H., obesity medicine physician and Men's Health advisor.

While there’s no way to lose fat from your midsection only without medical intervention, there are several ways to bring down your overall body fat which will pull from all areas. If losing your love handles is what will help boost your confidence and make you a healthier, happier version of yourself, that's a fine goal to have. Just remember that there's more to health than how you look, and you can set your sights on other outcomes, too (like getting stronger more generally or something like body recomposition more specifically).

LOVE HANDLES ARE what most people commonly call the bundle of subcutaneous fat that lies just above your pant line, sitting directly under the skin. That’s actually good news, because it means it’s not the dangerous kind of fat, called visceral fat, that can sit on your organs and put unnecessary (and life-threatening) pressure on them. Adipose fat, such as the love handles, can act as energy deposits. When our bodies lose other energy intake (food), we can use these deposits to power our bodily functions.

Even though our bodies have good intentions when collecting these love handles, it doesn’t mean they’re impossible to lose. But it will involve a solid calorie deficit and some effort in the gym.

There are a few shortcuts you can take, but they're extreme, and not something that we'd generally recommend. Liposuction is one of these options. More recently, men have turned to non-invasive treatments, the most popular of which feature either freezing or heating the stubborn fatty areas off the body. Some guys might also turn to using drugs like a GLP-1 (which can’t target one specific problem area), if a doctor recommends their use. These treatments are expensive and might be a bridge too far, unless you're really desperate.

Besides, by cutting corners, you'll miss out on the fitness gains you'd make along the way using other methods, which will hopefully become a reason you're training, regardless of the aesthetic payoff. If getting rid of love handles without special treatments is your goal, you'll have to work hard—and you'll have to work smart, too.

One method that is not smart and won't work is spot reduction. The theory is that if you focus all of your attention on one specific area in your training (for instance, doing hundreds of crunches for you midsection), you'll be able to burn off the fat in just that area.

But that's not how your body works. What you can do is lose fat more generally, then build up muscle where you might not have had it before—but for that to work, you'll have to do that smart, hard work. That’s also the case for GLP-1 use. If you go that route, make sure you understand how to train with a program like the MH GLP-1 Muscle Growth plan.

HERE’S A PLAN to ditch your stubborn love handles from former Men's Health fitness advisor Craig Ballantyne, C.S.C.S.

Studies have shown that interval-based exercise programs, most specifically high intensity interval training (HIIT), are more effective for burning off your love handles than steady state cardio. Instead of running for miles on end without any clear goal, fine tune your work and rest periods to strip away the fat.

So what type of interval program should you use? You can use a jump rope, or apply the principles to running or weight room work. Ballantyne recommends this setup to banish that pesky midsection fat:

After a thorough warmup, alternate between 20 seconds of hard exercise and 40 seconds recovery. Repeat that pattern 6 to 8 times. Afterwards, finish with 5 to 10 minutes of cooldown exercise.

If you have extra time, do 10 minutes of regular cardio pace.

Even though Ballantyne recommended cardio for a cool down, he's wary of its effectiveness when performed alone. Extended periods of steady state cardio, like jogging, won’t do much to cut down your spare tire. "It's not going to work as well as interval training," Ballantyne said.

This is related to another issue, according to Ballantyne: Many guys don't have enough muscle in the first place. Losing love handles, like bodybuilding, is a game of illusion. Muscle on your chest and back can essentially "hide" excess fat in your love handle area.

"So most guys are “skinny-fat,” and then try to lose love handles with cardio only, and basically become even smaller versions of themselves—but still skinny-fat," Ballantyne said. "It's better to use intervals and weight training to gain muscle and lose fat at the same time—which IS possible—and change your body's overall appearance."

"Ab exercises like crunches are generally a waste of time," Ballantyne said. The problem is, you’re only working the muscles around your lower spine with crunches and situps.

Instead, you should build up your core with moves that focus on spinal stability, like planks and hollow body holds. Check out this quick video about the way your core muscles function for an idea of what you should be aiming for:

Want a smarter core workout in general? Check out Epic Abs, the program from MH fitness director Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S. that inspired this video.

While you're cutting down your midsection, do yourself a solid and work on some other areas of your body that can take attention away from your ample hips. Build up your pecs, lats, deltoids, and traps to create the illusion of smaller love handles.

"Most guys don't have enough muscle to focus on just losing weight," Ballantyne said, "so every guy must build some muscle in these areas."

How can you build the muscle and lose fat at the same time? You're hoping to "culk," so you should start by training hard, eating properly, and sticking to a consistent program.

Ballantyne also recommended a plan based around two to three total body workouts per week. Use five exercises per workout (one lower body, one upper push, one lower body single leg, one upper pulling, one total body ab exercise). Do that as a circuit three times through, with eight to 12 reps per exercise. Finish with interval training.

For best results, follow a plan that fits your unique training needs. Use our Workout Finder below to get a personalized recommendation based on your age, fitness level, and other key factors.

You can't neglect nutrition if you're looking to lose fat. After all, losing fat means burning more calories then you take in, or creating a calorie deficit. Here’s how to calculate a healthy calorie deficit based on your body and goals.

There are easy eating hacks you can incorporate into your daily routine to cut calories while still enjoying yourself and staying satisfied. Eliminating foods you love is an unsustainable way to live. "Negotiate with yourself on what you are willing to do without or do with less of," says Leslie Bonci, R.D., sports dietitian for Kansas City Chiefs.

Prioritize and optimize protein, fiber, healthy fats, and produce to fill up. Protein and fiber help you stay fuller, longer—which may reduce snacking in between meals. When choosing grains, pick the higher fiber choices like quinoa, oatmeal, and whole wheat pastas. Incorporate more beans into your salads, soups, and even blend and add to sauces. Include a fruit or a veggie at every occasion.

When it comes to snacking, focus on foods that will make you chew longer and eat slower, like jerky or apples. Bean dips with veggies are also a quick and easy snack that will load up the fiber and protein with little calories.

To really find a custom nutrition plan that will work best with your body, talk to a registered dietitian.

We don’t need to tell you that losing weight is no walk in the park. Accomplishing your goals will take a balance of overhauled nutrition, exercise, and recovery practices to complete the equation and finally shed some of those pounds. You might find it tough to do any of those things on your own.

Working with a professional can help provide some much needed accountability and guidance. Doctors who specialize in weight loss, nutritionists, dietitians, and personal trainers can all help you get to where you want to be. They can tailor your workouts and meal plans to better match your genetic makeup and goals. Don’t be afraid to ask for help if the task feels daunting.

SORRY TO BREAK it to you—doing loads of side bends and Russian twists won’t melt away your love handles. It’s impossible to lose fat on one portion of your body by exercising the muscles in that area. The concept is called spot training, or spot reduction—and it doesn’t work.

What does work is incorporating high-velocity compound movements into your workouts. Compound movements are exercises that require multiple muscle groups working together. These kinds of moves will burn a lot of calories, aiding in creating the calorie deficit you need to burn fat all over. Here are 6 of our favorites.

This move lights up your body head to toe, and ramps up your heart rate in the process. Not only will med ball slams aid in the fat loss process, but they’ll help you take a little aggression out on your worst days.

Sets and Reps: Aim for 2 to 3 sets of 30 second sets, either as a warm up or programmed into your next conditioning circuit.

The dumbbell snatch is one of the best movements for building full body power and strength. Almost your entire body has to work to power the weight up and overhead.

Sets and Reps: Aim for 3 sets of 3 to 5 reps with a heavy weight, or build it into a conditioning set by doing 30 seconds of work, 30 seconds of rest with a medium weight.

The kettlebell swing is a fundamental core exercise that works practically every muscle in your body. Be careful about ramping up the weight too quickly though—this move has a ton of subtleties that are vital to the safety of the movement.

Sets and Reps: Do 4 sets of 10 to 12 reps with a heavy weight, or build it into a conditioning set by doing 30 seconds of work, 30 seconds of rest with a medium weight.

Burpees are infamous for a reason. It looks simple, but do it the right way and you’ll feel way more of a challenge than you’d expect.

Sets and Reps: Aim 3 to 4 rounds of 20 seconds on, 40 seconds off, or build it into a conditioning circuit.

Mountain climbers are a staple core exercise that will challenge your upper body too as you maintain that high plank position.

Sets and Reps: Set a timer for 6 minutes and aim for 20 seconds of work, 10 seconds of rest for a good core burn, build it into a conditioning circuit.

This multi-joint movement combines a front squat and a push press to incorporate the whole body to build power and strength—and torch calories, too.

Sets and Reps: Aim for 3 sets of 6 to 8 reps, build it into a conditioning circuit for 30 seconds of work, 30 seconds of rest.

The platform combines crypto perpetual futures, including Bitcoin and Ethereum, with xStocks instruments tracking companies such as Apple, NVIDIA and Tesla, alongside stock-index ETFs. Positions across the markets share the same account balance and count toward the same evaluation. Traders can work across crypto and equity-linked instruments in one terminal while managing a single set of account limits.

A WSDT challenge tests trading performance against a 10% profit target, a 4% daily loss limit and a 6% maximum drawdown fixed against the starting account size. #5251. Why Bitcoin Just Dropped to a 5-Month Low Near $61,300

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Why Bitcoin Just Dropped to a 5-Month Low Near $61,300

Three separate market pressures just collided—pushing BTC to a level not seen since July.

Bitcoin plunged 4.35% over the past 24 hours, falling to $61,300 — its lowest level since early July — as a global sell-off in AI stocks, heavy withdrawals from Bitcoin ETFs and a wave of forced liquidations sent shockwaves through crypto markets.

By Friday morning, Bitcoin was struggling to stay above $61,500, putting it on track for its seventh consecutive weekly decline.

This drop wasn’t triggered by a single event. Instead, several pressures hit the market at once: growing concerns over AI valuations, institutional investors pulling money out of Bitcoin ETFs, and leveraged traders being forced to close their positions as prices fell.

The broader pullback was driven by a retreat from riskier assets as investors questioned lofty AI valuations.

On Thursday, November 19, AI company Anthropic made its highly anticipated debut on the Nasdaq. Shares opened at $111.50 against an IPO price of $83, briefly pushing the company’s valuation above $2 trillion. However, the successful IPO failed to lift sentiment across the technology sector.

As Anthropic began trading, Bitcoin fell from around $62,700 to $62,250 within roughly 30 minutes, while broader Nasdaq losses accelerated.

By the end of the session, the Nasdaq was down 2.3%, the S&P 500 had fallen 2%, and the Dow Jones lost 2.2%.

The sell-off spread to Asia, where South Korea’s KOSPI dropped approximately 5%, triggering a temporary restriction on automated selling.

Institutional demand for Bitcoin is also showing signs of weakening, adding further pressure to an already struggling market.

According to SoSoValue data, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $582.19 million in net outflows on November 19, marking the largest single-day withdrawal of the month.

With the exception of a modest $8 million inflow on November 5, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have faced nearly two weeks of persistent capital withdrawals, signaling a significant pullback in institutional demand.

As spot prices broke below key support levels, leveraged derivatives traders fueled a cascade of forced selling.

CoinGlass data shows $697.35 million in crypto positions were liquidated over the past 24 hours. About $600M came from long positions, and $201.25M of the total was Bitcoin longs.

According to market analyst Axel Adler Jr., Bitcoin remains under significant bearish pressure, with short-term investors sitting on substantial unrealized losses. Bitcoin is currently trading 15.7% below the average cost basis of recent buyers and has remained below that level for 12 consecutive days.

Until BTC reclaims the short-term holder cost basis and U.S. spot ETF flows flip back into positive territory, an analyst warns that the broader market correction isn’t over yet.

Bitcoin’s slide alongside AI stocks underscores how tightly crypto still tracks risk appetite in traditional markets. Continued ETF outflows and leveraged liquidations are likely to keep pressure on prices until broader market sentiment stabilizes.

#5250. Eight Years: From a Crypto Exchange to a Global Ecosystem Serving 40 Million Users

What started eight years ago as a cryptocurrency exchange has evolved into an international business ecosystem of 11 companies serving approximately 40 million users worldwide. As WhiteBIT celebrates its eighth anniversary and W Group marks its first year, the milestones highlight a transformation from a single trading platform into a diversified business connecting traditional finance, digital assets, and emerging technologies.

The scale of this growth is reflected in WhiteBIT’s $2.8 trillion trading volume in 2026 and more than 5,500 institutional clients. Meanwhile, W Group has expanded from eight to 11 companies in one year, growing its combined user base from 35 million to approximately 40 million.

Established in 2025, W Group brought together businesses developed around WhiteBIT under a broader strategy: connecting traditional finance and digital assets while extending their applications into new industries.

The group aims to build more than a portfolio of independent companies. By combining financial infrastructure, technology and expertise, its businesses can develop new services, reach new markets and create opportunities across industries.

In 2026, W Group expanded well beyond financial services. Dutch sports car manufacturer Spyker joined the group in June, opening opportunities to apply digital finance and blockchain technology to luxury automotive.

W Group has also made a $400 million investment commitment in SignSplit, the signed-data platform for the AI era. The seed round values SignSplit at $1 billion.

In banking, Georgia-based hashbank, a fully licensed digital bank, combines traditional banking services with cryptocurrency functionality, allowing customers to manage fiat and digital assets within one environment.

Together, these businesses illustrate W Group’s strategy of connecting financial services, technology, and consumer-facing products into an ecosystem where each company can contribute to the growth of the others.

WhiteBIT remains a central pillar of W Group, providing trading infrastructure and digital asset services for retail and institutional clients.

In 2026, the exchange recorded $2.8 trillion in trading volume, with derivatives generating approximately $3.5 billion in daily activity. Its platform now offers nearly 1,200 trading markets.

Trading conditions have also improved. Spot trading volume across WhiteBIT’s flagship BTC, ETH and WBT pairs increased more than fivefold, from $53 billion in 2020 to $276 billion in 2025. Meanwhile, bid-ask spreads across its major markets have narrowed approximately threefold since 2021, reflecting deeper liquidity.

WhiteBIT also serves more than 5,500 institutional clients, including funds, brokers and payment providers, through over 20 dedicated products and services. Businesses can access crypto liquidity, manage digital asset transactions and move between fiat currencies and cryptocurrencies through a single platform.

WhiteBIT’s eighth year brought significant regulatory milestones that strengthen the group’s international presence.

In June 2026, WhiteBIT EU secured authorisation under the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) from Austria’s Financial Market Authority, establishing a regulatory foundation for providing crypto-asset services across the European Union.

In May, WhiteBIT launched a dedicated platform for users in the United Kingdom, expanding into another major financial market with demanding regulatory requirements. The company also joined Ghana’s regulatory sandbox in March, contributing to the development of the country’s digital asset regulatory framework.

These developments reflect WhiteBIT’s investment in compliance as a foundation for sustainable international growth.

The growth of the ecosystem is also reflected in WBT, WhiteBIT’s native coin, which reached an all-time high of nearly $88 in September 2026, up from its launch price of $1.62 in 2022.*The milestone reflects WBT’s strong long-term performance alongside the expansion of WhiteBIT and its ecosystem.

WBT’s role is also expanding beyond trading. In November, Whitechain transitioned into an Ethereum Layer 2 network built on the OP Stack in partnership with Optimism, with WBT used to pay transaction fees. Designed to support blockchain applications and financial services, Whitechain has already attracted interest from developers, with more than 140 teams applying to its Builders Program ahead of the network’s public launch planned for later in November.

For W Group, the next stage of growth will focus on connecting its businesses more closely and turning their combined capabilities into new products and services.

“Eight years ago, we started with one cryptocurrency exchange. Today, we’ve grown into an international group of 11 companies serving around 40 million users. But our ambition has never been simply to build more businesses. We want to connect them in ways that create real value — bringing traditional finance and digital assets closer together, making new technologies more accessible and opening opportunities across industries,” said Volodymyr Nosov, Founder and President of W Group.

Looking ahead, W Group aims to strengthen its presence in regulated markets, expand institutional financial services and accelerate blockchain infrastructure development. Its long-term vision is an interconnected ecosystem where banking, payments, digital assets and emerging technologies work together, making financial services more accessible to people and businesses worldwide.

Brandt's latest doomsday prediction comes at a time when Bitcoin is still trying to recover from its biggest sell-off to date, which has wiped out close to half of its market value from its October 2025 peak.

The trader's latest post on X highlights a pattern he has found throughout Bitcoin's price history: previous bull runs have always ended with devastating market corrections.

"Every bull market phase in the history of BTC has ended with at least a 75% correction of the prior parabolic bull trend," Brandt's X post reads.

Continuing his warning, Brandt raised an alarming question: "Is this what is happening with Bitcoin?"

The trading veteran has not put a number on the possible crash. But his words point toward the possibility that the current drop in Bitcoin might be part of a larger correction and not just a temporary dip.

These historic crashes have shown the extreme losses that Bitcoin investors have faced during such market corrections.

At the time of writing on Nov. 20, Bitcoin is currently trading at around $62,000, which is almost 51% below its October 2025 all-time high.

If it were to undergo a 75% price correction from its all-time high, then it would drop to around $31,550.

But it's worth mentioning that Brandt referred to a correction of the prior parabolic bull trend, which may not be the same as a 75% correction from the peak.

Interestingly enough, this is not the first time the trader has warned about an even darker future for Bitcoin's price.

Earlier, on Nov. 15, Brandt shared a weekly BTC chart showing a potential head-and-shoulders formation, a technical pattern that usually signals a bearish reversal.

According to Brandt, if the pattern is confirmed, there's a chance that Bitcoin could never revisit its previous all-time high in his lifetime.

The chart he shared also indicates an important zone between $60,000 and $65,000. A confirmed breakdown below this zone could further strengthen the bearish outlook.

Moreover, there is still plenty of selling pressure in the crypto market. The latest update from Lookonchain on Nov. 19 revealed that U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs had seen net outflows of around $975 million over the past seven days. The biggest net outflows came from BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT).

#5247. Cardano’s $5M conference budget has a $1M problem — Details!

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

The Cardano [ADA] Treasury Foundation wants 25 million ADA to host 12 events in 2027. Its last $22 million proposal (to buy copper) barely got any votes at all.

Hence, the question — Will this one fare any better?

On 16th November, the Cardano Foundation filed a proposal to pull 24,995,775 ADA from the network’s treasury. The money would pay for Cardano’s presence at 12 crypto events next year.

Some of the biggest names on the circuit are on the list. Consensus in Miami, TOKEN2049 in both Singapore and New York, Web Summit in Lisbon, and India Blockchain Week in Bangalore.

The run kicks off in February with the Africa Tech Summit in Nairobi.

$2 million will go towards sponsorships and $1.06 million for booths and equipment. Travel is said to cost $702K, while side events will account for $695,000.

According to the Foundation, none of it covers salaries or profit. Whatever isn’t spent goes back to the treasury.

However, here’s what’s tricky. The Foundation priced ADA at $0.20 to reach its $5 million budget. ADA, however, was valued at $0.15 at press time. At that price, the request is worth about $3.85 million. That is a gap of over $1 million.

For the budget to work as planned, ADA needs to climb by almost 30%. Not impossible, but far from guaranteed.

DReps, the delegates who vote on treasury spending, have until 20th December to decide.

Will 25 million ADA move the price? Probably not. There are about 37.6 billion ADA in circulation. So, this withdrawal will merely be a drop in the ocean.

However, it’s worth pointing out that the chart had bigger problems at press time.

ADA fell from $0.25 in October to $0.155 following a price drop on the 14th.

Is a pause imminent? We might be in the early stages, yes. The RSI fell to 21 after that drop, with the same since climbing to 32, just crossing above its average. The OI has also recovered from about $145 million to $153.5 million. Finally, the funding rates were positive yesterday.

On the contrary, the Chaikin Money Flow was negative, implying that sellers might still have a slight edge.

#5246. Worse Than 2008? Peter Schiff Issues Terrifying Market Crash Warning

Noted economist and longtime Bitcoin critic Peter Schiff has sounded the alarm about an upcoming financial apocalypse, warning that the crisis could be worse than the historic 2008 market crash.

On Nov. 20, Peter Schiff shared a series of troubling X posts warning about the potential for significant losses in the U.S. stock market, real estate, and cryptocurrencies amid escalating financial system stress.

The economist shared a video with a very alarming headline: "The Next Crash Will Be Worse Than 2008."

In one of his most recent posts on X, Schiff argued that the recent gold price downtrend might signal a grim outlook for other key asset classes.

"It's probably a bad sign that gold is falling this much. It probably means that the stock and real estate markets are going to fall even more in percentage terms," Schiff cautioned.

According to Peter Schiff, gold's recent price behavior could be signaling deflation. As a result, this might lead to a more severe financial crisis.

However, Peter Schiff is convinced that the Federal Reserve will step in to prevent this financial apocalypse.

"Gold is signaling deflation. But asset deflation would bust the government and the banking system, so the Fed will pivot to avoid it," the economist explained.

Simply put, Schiff assumes that the Federal Reserve will pivot and introduce monetary stimulus to prevent a financial meltdown.

In another startling prediction, the economist warned that the U.S. stock market might wipe out all its gains since President Donald Trump took office.

"There's a good chance that the U.S. stock market is about to give back all the gains since Trump took office," the economist predicted.

He also warned that there might be a recession. As a result, Trump will likely point to Democrats and their wins in the recent midterm elections as the reason for this recession.

Interestingly enough, Peter Schiff's bearish outlook also applies to Bitcoin (BTC), which has already suffered significant losses amid the overall market crash.

On Nov. 18, Peter Schiff shared several alarming market indicators. According to his data, the Nasdaq has dropped 12.25%. AI infrastructure company CoreWeave has plummeted 64%.

Bitcoin, on the other hand, has plunged 33.5% from its 2026 peak.

Additionally, the economist noted that the U.S. housing market index had dropped to 25, its lowest level since 2012. This shows that the economic issues go well beyond AI stocks.

"Still think this is just about AI?" he asked.

Toronto, November 19, 2026 – OmenX, a Base-native leveraged prediction market platform, today announced $2 million in funding from Informed Ventures alongside the launch of its on-demand, 30-second Bitcoin price prediction product.

The new product lets users predict whether Bitcoin’s price will rise or fall over the next 30 seconds, with each trade starting its own prediction window. A position opened at 10:00:12 runs until 10:00:42. Users can act when their view forms, with a full 30-second horizon, rather than adapting to the remaining time in a shared market round.

Featuring zero-slippage execution and rapid settlement, the product extends the familiar five- and fifteen-minute crypto prediction format to a shorter, individually timed experience. It adds to OmenX’s intraday offering, which spans prediction horizons from 30 seconds to 24 hours, depending on the market.

Beyond crypto, OmenX offers directional prediction markets linked to more than 100 global assets, including U.S. equities, futures, ETFs and indices. Its event markets also cover live sports and esports, with sports coverage spanning major football leagues, basketball, American football, ice hockey, baseball and UFC.

Leverage has been central to OmenX’s platform from the outset, allowing traders to amplify their exposure on supported event markets. The latest launch builds on that foundation while advancing a broader goal: making prediction markets a practical financial tool for retail users.

OmenX organizes the trading decision around a defined question: will an asset’s price be higher or lower at the end of a specified period? Users can express a directional view without purchasing the underlying asset, targeting an exact closing price or constructing an options position that requires decisions about strikes, implied volatility and time decay.

“Leverage has been part of OmenX from the start, but our ambition goes beyond adding leverage to prediction markets,” said James, founder and CEO of OmenX. “We want to make global markets easier to participate in. A trader should be able to take a view on Bitcoin, a stock or a sporting event and express it through a clear contract and a timeframe that fits their judgment.”

The platform’s emphasis on short, recurring markets provides faster feedback on trading decisions and can reduce the time capital remains committed to individual outcomes. OmenX plans to expand its coverage of traditional and crypto assets while deepening the trading experience across supported markets.

OmenX is a Base-native leveraged prediction market platform covering crypto, global financial assets, live sports and esports. Through defined outcomes, short settlement cycles and leverage on supported markets, OmenX is building a more accessible way to trade market views.

#5244. GTA VI Launch Sparks $250M Solana Stock Frenzy Over Nvidia

Home » Altcoins » Solana (SOL) » GTA VI Launch Sparks $250M Solana Stock Frenzy Over Nvidia

Tokenized Take-Two shares saw a massive 24-hour trading spike as on-chain markets attract Washington scrutiny.

The long-awaited release of Grand Theft Auto VI didn’t just break gaming records—it briefly turned publisher Take-Two Interactive into the hottest stock on the blockchain, outselling even AI giant Nvidia.

On November 18, decentralized exchange (DEX) trading volume for tokenized Take-Two shares (TTWO) exploded by 578%, jumping from $36.8 million to $249.5 million in a single day, according to Token Terminal data.

That was roughly 2.8 times the $88.1 million traded in tokenized Nvidia (NVDA) shares over the same 24-hour window, accounting for 42% of all on-chain stock trading.

Nearly all of the action, roughly $239 million, or 96% of total volume, happened on Solana via Backpack Securities, a subsidiary of crypto exchange Backpack. Launched earlier this year, the token is designed to be backed 1:1 by real Take-Two shares held in custody.

Traditional Wall Street traders saw a much calmer reaction: Take-Two’s Nasdaq shares rose 6.2% to close at $216.61 on launch day before pulling back 3.7% to $208.65 the next session.

Despite Take-Two’s one-day viral spike, Nvidia remains the undisputed heavyweight of tokenized equities, boasting a $399.4 million market cap and $2 billion in 30-day trading volume (compared to Take-Two’s $808.1 million).

Overall, tokenized public stocks on Solana have nearly doubled since late October to reach $1.22 billion.

That rapid growth is drawing fresh scrutiny in Washington. On November 16, four Democratic senators sent a letter to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) questioning how its newly introduced exemption for tokenized securities would address investor protection and anti-money laundering requirements.

The issue also surfaced during the November 19 Senate Banking Committee confirmation hearing for Kristin Johnson, President Donald Trump’s nominee for the SEC. Johnson indicated that exemptions covering tokenized stocks should eventually be formalized through rules following a public comment period.

The TTWO spike shows tokenized stocks can attract event-driven trading on-chain, comparable to some of the largest names in the segment. It also coincides with growing regulatory scrutiny of how tokenized stocks are supervised.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Hong Kong has just put Hyperliquid [HYPE] on its watchlist. And yet, traders don’t seem to be bothered.

In fact, on Hyperliquid itself, the action is only heating up now.

On Wednesday, Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) added Hyperliquid to its Alert List. The problem cited was that they don’t hold a licence to operate in the city.

The regulator’s entry covers two names; Hyperliquid and Hyperliquid Hong Kong. It also shared the exchange’s trading website. It is believed that the platform may be serving Hong Kong users, presenting itself as a local operator, or pitching its services to people in the city.

With this addition, the SFC’s list of suspicious crypto trading platforms has grown to 69 names now. At the time of writing, Hyperliquid hadn’t commented on the development.

Back in June, Singapore’s central bank placed Hyperliquid on its Investor Alert List which flags firms people might wrongly assume are regulated there. At the time, Hyperliquid’s response was simple — it never said it had a Singapore licence.

Now, there are two Asian financial hubs keeping an eye on the exchange.

While Hong Kong was flagging Hyperliquid, traders on the platform were busy betting on Anthropic.

On 18th November, the number of traders holding long positions on Anthropic perps hit a record 5,567.

A week ago, that figure was 2,926; nearly doubling in seven days. There were 1,996 short holders, with the same hinting at 2.8 longs for every short.

Most of that action was on Trade[XYZ]’s ANT market. According to Token Terminal, this alone accounted for 4,190 long holders,.

One caveat, though. These numbers count traders, not the size of their bets. And since the data adds up three markets, anyone trading on two of them gets counted twice.

The altcoin was trading at $67.66, at press time, following a hike of just 1% in the last 24 hours. Its price was still a long way from its late-October levels when it briefly climbed above $95. Since then, it’s been mostly downhill for the crypto.

There seemed to be some sign of a breather though. The RSI was below 30 during that drop. It has since come back to just nudging above its average.

The CMF at -0.06 suggested that sellers still had the upper hand, but the outflows were clearly weaker than earlier this month.

Bitcoin (BTC) price continues to fall as the sell-off from the $86,000 - $87,000 region in October is gathering momentum. The sell-off has accelerated in recent days, and BTC price has slipped to roughly $61,900, moving closer to the next technical support level at $60,000.

The daily chart shows several concerning technical developments for Bitcoin. Shorter-term moving averages continue to fall below longer-term moving averages, forming a technical pattern commonly known as a death cross. The death cross has now formed twice with 100 and 200 EMAs, indicating a worsening technical setup for Bitcoin, commonly known as a double death cross.

Several key moving averages continue to cluster in the $75,000 - $76,000 region, adding resistance for Bitcoin price action.

Relative Strength Index (RSI) has started to move closer to the oversold region, indicating that momentum has started to slow for Bitcoin.

Taken together, this technical setup indicates that selling pressure for Bitcoin has been increasing on multiple time frames. We are monitoring $60,000 as a key support level. This level was also an area of interest for buyers during the June correction in Bitcoin.

Should BTC price continue to move lower and break out below $60,000, the next level of support to watch will be $58,000, followed by $56,000.

For Bitcoin price to reverse course and show signs of a meaningful short-term rebound, it will need to continue higher and break out above $64,000 - $65,000.

Breaking out above $68,000 would be a strong move that could help to stabilize Bitcoin in the short term. A positive move for Bitcoin would need to continue higher and reclaim several key moving averages. Until then, Bitcoin will continue to trade in a more bearish technical setup.

Bitcoin price action continues to move lower on the daily chart. All technical indicators on this chart continue to deteriorate, indicating that Bitcoin remains vulnerable to another leg lower before buyers can show signs of a robust short-term recovery.

#5240. Bitcoin’s $700M liquidation wave deepens – Is crypto’s $2T market cap at risk?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Anthropic’s post-IPO performance appears to have created a volatile market setup.

On the technical side, ANT opened at $111.50, around 34% above its $83 IPO price, before losing much of its early gains and closing at $97.17. This shows that initial demand was strong, but profit-taking quickly kicked in. The impact also seems to have spilled over into crypto, with the total market cap forming its third consecutive lower low at $2.08 trillion, a level last seen in early Q3.

Naturally, this raises a question: Is crypto’s weakness simply a result of ANT-driven volatility? Interestingly, recent Glassnode data points to a possible link. As the chart below shows, Anthropic futures on crypto platforms recorded $9.5 billion in trading volume ahead of its Nasdaq debut. In comparison, SpaceX, the largest IPO on record, attracted $3.9 billion in pre-listing futures volume before its June debut.

In essence, ANT’s pre-IPO futures generated more than 2.4x SpaceX’s.

This highlights how much larger speculative interest in ANT was compared to SpaceX, setting a new record for pre-IPO trading activity on crypto platforms. However, the initial hype quickly turned into profit-taking, with ANT dropping 13% from its opening price. This shift in sentiment may have added to Bitcoin’s [BTC] selling pressure, especially as liquidation activity picked up alongside the broader market breakdown.

So, is Bitcoin’s latest breakdown the start of an overall deleveraging process in crypto markets? In other words, could IPO-driven volatility have accelerated long liquidations, forced overleveraged traders out of positions, and triggered a general market reset?

It looks like ANT’s futures activity on crypto platforms may have added to the selling pressure.

According to CoinGlass, over $700 million worth of positions have been liquidated in the last 24 hours. Of that amount, nearly $600 million was long positions, indicating that leveraged bulls have been badly hit by the correction. However, can this flush-out in Futures markets lead to a rebalance?

Worth mentioning here is the ongoing liquidity drain. In the last 30 days, $11.5 billion has left the stablecoin supply. That outflow is greater than it was in the aftermath of the Terra collapse in 2022. While many in the crypto market are looking at Bitcoin’s price movements, the real problem is the decreasing capital in crypto.

Why does this matter? Lower stablecoin supply means less available liquidity to support buying activity, which could keep pressure on Bitcoin and the broader market.

So, while ANT-related volatility may have contributed to market deleveraging, liquidity is still very poor for a sustained recovery. In this context, ANT’s IPO may have added to an already fragile market, while concerns around its valuation may also “continue” to create a risk-off sentiment in U.S. markets.

Against this backdrop, a drop in the total crypto market cap below $2 trillion cannot be ruled out.

ANT’s IPO may have added to Bitcoin’s fear and increased crypto selling.

Weak liquidity could keep pressure on crypto, putting the $2 trillion market cap at risk.

"Rich Dad Poor Dad" author Robert Kiyosaki wrote on X on Nov. 20 that he is "most excited about Bitcoin's crash" and is "waiting to buy more." On the same day, Bitcoin was trading at $61,666, more than 50% below its October 2025 peak of about $126,000.

Gold fell 1.24% to $3,579 an ounce, and silver lost 0.95% to $42.42, according to TradingView data. The S&P 500 dropped 2.02% on the same day.

Kiyosaki started his post with a question. "CRASH: Good or Bad? Gold, silver, Bitcoin, crashing. Weak hands selling. Strong hands waiting to buy?" he wrote.

According to Kiyosaki, the reasons include "incompetence in FED, Banks, and Bond markets." He also wrote that America's debt is "only to grow bigger" as "Banksters steal our wealth via their system legally."

The author pointed to Bitcoin's fixed supply. There will be only 21 million BTC in total, and about 20 million coins have already been mined, Kiyosaki wrote. "As far as I know, there has never been a 'money' such as Bitcoin ever before," he added.

"With price of Bitcoin crashing, I can't wait to buy more coins… just because only 21 million are ever to be mined. It could be a 'nothing burger'…. or the best money I've ever spent," Kiyosaki wrote.

In late August, Kiyosaki said on podcasts that he owed creditors $1.2 billion. His ex-wife and business partner, Kim Kiyosaki, later said that the figure covered the loans of a partnership that owns about 1,500 rental units. "We have a lot of apartment houses with our partners," she said.

According to Kim Kiyosaki, Robert Kiyosaki's own share of the debt is $30 million to $60 million. Each of their real estate investments is held in a separate LLC. Robert Kiyosaki also commented on the debt at the time. "If it all comes to hell, you can talk to my attorney," he said.

In 2012, Kiyosaki's company Rich Global LLC filed for bankruptcy after a court ordered it to pay about $24 million.

The crypto market’s current downfall is primarily due to persistent Spot ETF outflows and lingering fallout from last month’s Binance breach, which are making investors wary.

As the global cryptocurrency market cap fell 2.2% to $2.21 trillion in the last 24 hours at press time, the Crypto Fear & Greed Index slid to 12, indicating “extreme fear.”

After $306.5 million left Spot Bitcoin ETFs on the 18th of November, CoinGlass data showed that $582.3 million in outflows on the following day,  pushing this month’s outflows well past the $2.9 billion mark. Continued ETF bleeding signals that buyers continue to exit, leaving the market quite vulnerable to macro volatility.

Similarly, minutes from the October FOMC meeting, released on the 18th of November, showed that nearly all officials expect further rate hikes. Notably, Governor Christopher Waller even floated a half-point move for December.

With the Fed target at 3.75%–4.00%, digital assets will not have an easy battle.

Ever since investors have moved away from crypto and into AI, the former’s fall has been nearly constant. For the uninitiated, on the 18th of November, Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, thus valuing the AI company at roughly $1.5 trillion.

The news drew massive investor attention, pulling capital away from crypto markets as a result.

Regardless, the long-term sentiment of crypto investors has already been sullied due to the October 29 Binance hack that resulted in $6.3 billion in stolen funds.

The crypto bloodbath will likely continue unless ETF flows stabilize or the Fed signals a pause. With the December 9 FOMC meeting as the only upcoming checkpoint, 60,000 is the next level for traders to watch. Losing it can tip Bitcoin deeper into the mid-50,000s.

#5235. BlackRock Records Largest Bitcoin Outflow in History

BlackRock, the leading asset management firm and Bitcoin’s largest ETF issuer, sparked discussions earlier today following a massive Bitcoin sale by the company.

The latest data showcased by SosoValue shows that the leading Bitcoin fund has witnessed massive single-day withdrawals from investors who have ventured into its Bitcoin investment product.

Earlier today, BlackRock sold over half a billion dollars’ worth of Bitcoin after its spot Bitcoin ETF, also known as iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), recorded a total of $541.08 million in net outflows.

This massive outflow has come as Bitcoin’s price decline continues to intensify, causing investors to aggressively pull their money out of the fund amid growing market fear.

While this marks the third time this week that BlackRock has recorded a net outflow amid persistent market volatility, it also marks the largest single-day outflow BlackRock has recorded since its launch.

Apparently, the record-breaking withdrawal that the fund just witnessed suggests that institutional and traditional investors are becoming less willing to retain their exposure to Bitcoin through asset managers, especially as Bitcoin’s price continues to slump further.

Although BlackRock has just suffered the largest withdrawal since it launched its Bitcoin investment product, the record outflow did not alter its dominance in the market.

Further data shows that the BlackRock spot Bitcoin ETF still boasts a massive $47.82 billion in assets under management, spotlighting its leadership in the Bitcoin ETF market.

This positions it far ahead of Fidelity, which ranks as the second-largest Bitcoin ETF with just $10.62 billion in net assets.

#5234. The Best Winter Jackets for Men, Tested by Style Editors

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

We tried more than 40 options to find the ones worth wearing all season.

MEN’S HEALTH EDITORS spend a lot of time outdoors. We commute to our NYC office, then juggle the gym, errands, and weekend outings. So when cold weather hits, we need winter coats that can get us through nearly every icy scenario imaginable. Gone are the days when staying warm meant looking like a walking snowman. Today’s outerwear pairs advanced insulation with weather-resistant fabrics and thoughtful details to help keep you warm when the temperatures drop. The best designs layer comfortably, move well, and still look sharp.

As someone who tests gear year-round—and as part of a team that’s been reviewing winter coats since 2019—I’ve worn everything from lightweight puffers on frosty commutes to parkas in sub-zero conditions. Along the way, the Men’s Health style team has put more than 40 coats through real-life use: daily city commutes, snowy trail days, and ski trips. We look at how warm they actually feel, how well they move, how tough the materials are, and whether they look good off the rack. And after all that, Mack Weldon, Columbia, and Canada Goose rose to the top as the best winter coats for men.

I’ve been getting my wear out of Mack Weldon’s WarmKnit Air Hooded Jacket for the past year and it surprised me with its performance. At first glance, you’d think it’s just a lightweight puffer built for those mild 50- to 60-degree temps. But I found it could hang in the 40s, too—and still keep me warm. That’s thanks to its Thinsulate fill, synthetic insulation made of ultra-fine fibers, which does the heavy lifting without making me feel like a bloated marshmallow. It’s water- and wind-resistant, so a little drizzle or gusty wind doesn’t ruin a commute either.

The snap-button front and the two-way zipper make it easy to get in and out of, and the structured hood actually stays put, protecting your head without flopping around or blowing off. Just like most of Mack Weldon’s winter collection, sporty casual meets performance is the vibe here, so you can wear it with anything from a sweatsuit to a casual crewneck over chinos. With bonded quilting and interior pockets, it's both functional and polished, so it works for weekend hikes or casual dinners.

That said, there are trade‑offs. The jacket’s waist‑length cut means it won’t cover your core the way a mid‑thigh parka does, so in truly cold winter conditions you’ll feel more exposed around hips and lower back. If you need serious warmth for winter storms, opt for a longer cut; if you want a versatile everyday coat for mild to moderately cold weather, this is a standout value pick.

For days when you want warmth without the bulk, this Columbia down jacket delivers in spades. It uses Omni‑Heat reflective lining—those tiny silver dots that bounce your body heat back at you—which helps keep heat where you want it even as temperatures dip and winds pick up. It’s the kind of jacket you reach for when you want to feel cozy without feeling weighed down.

The 650‑fill down has enough loft to stay warm without ballooning your silhouette, and the baffle construction keeps insulation evenly distributed while creating a streamlined look that’s more polished than many puffers of similar warmth. Columbia also packs in tech‑forward features like HeatSeal construction to trap warmth while still allowing breathability and Omni‑Shield for moisture resistance and stain repellency—handy when you’re trudging through slush or, as I once did, surviving a spilled coffee on the way to the bus.

What I appreciate most is how easily it layers: It slips over a fleece or hoodie without feeling stiff, and it’s comfortable enough to wear all day whether you’re heading to work or exploring snowy trails. It’s not the warmest jacket around, but for everyday winter conditions where you want mobility and comfort with insulation, it’s a fantastic pick.

This is, quite simply, one of the best budget winter jackets we’ve tested—and it’s worth your attention even if you usually steer clear of ultra‑affordable picks. Deals and Trends Editor Tim Kohut wore the coat zipped up, and found that the heavyweight insulation did a solid job at keeping the shivers at bay on a brisk walk to the train — all without overheating once he hit the warm subway platform.

The polyester shell is water-repellent, not waterproof, so he can survive light showers without them soaking through to his clothes. It may not be the best option for heavy rain, so if you’re staring down a prolonged rainstorm, an umbrella or rain layer is still a smart call. Its relaxed fit is roomy enough for you to fit a chunky sweater underneath without bulk. Kohut rocked a T-shirt and chunky cardigan, and did not feel like the Michelin Man after being fully zipped up. The hood doesn’t cinch tight — one of the few real drawbacks — which lets cold air sneak in on windier days, but it is fleece‑lined for extra comfort and warmth.

Pockets are straightforward but functional, and the simple styling means this jacket works for daily commuting as easily as casual weekends. For the price, it’s a total win if you want something warm, reliable, and unfussy without dropping big cash.

Our Grooming Editor Sean Zucker wore this parka in every cold-weather situation: long commutes, chilly hikes, snowball fights. It has a slim puffer design but with a longer cut and more down, making it warmer for bone-chilling morning walks to the coffee shop. Zucker recently got caught in a sudden downpour, and the waterproof—not just water-resistant—shell kept him completely dry. On a freezing 30-degree cold and windy day, he stayed warm and comfortable the entire time. Plus, the storm cuffs blocked icy gusts from sneaking in at the sleeves.

He also appreciated the two-way zipper, which you don’t see on a lot of winter coats. It made hopping on and off the subway or sitting at a café easy without feeling restricted. While the insulated hood isn’t super spacious, it cinches close enough to trap heat. The fit is stylish without feeling bulky, and his hands fit perfectly in the pockets—small detail, but it really makes a difference when it’s freezing out. Yes, it’s an investment piece, but with premium 700-fill down warmth, waterproof and windproof protection, and thoughtful features, this parka is a true workhorse built to handle harsh conditions.

Canada Goose’s coat may come with some sticker shock, but our Style and Reviews Director Christian Gollayan has made good use of it for the past three winters. He wears it to walk his two corgis, and between the snow, wind, and icy sidewalks, it keeps him warm without feeling like he’s lugging around a heavy sleeping bag. The Arctic Tech fabric—a polyester-cotton blend—has structure without stiffness, so it handles those brutal days when the wind tries to cut straight through you. Its longer silhouette offers extra coverage in snowy conditions. Not to mention, it’s a stylish coat, so you’re getting warmth and thoughtful design versus a bulky, shapeless puffer.

Like Fjallraven’s parka, this one has more pockets than your average coat—four outside, three inside. Two are great for thawing frozen mitts, and the others have flaps that help secure smaller essentials like a wallet, beanie, or winter gloves. There’s even a down-filled hood that feels toasty without making you feel stuffy, plus backpack-style straps if you want to carry it hands-free while running errands or grabbing coffee.

Sure, it’s very pricey, but we had to bite the bullet and think about the bigger picture. Stepping outside doesn’t feel like wrestling with the elements anymore. Between warmth, thoughtful design, and sleek style, it’s become our go-to armor for extreme weather—and it’s already survived three ruthless winter seasons in a row.

Men’s Health designer Jason Speakman took this burly parka from Fjallraven out on the slopes during a trip to Aspen. At 6 feet tall with a slender build, he found that this jacket wasn’t suffocating or too heavy, letting him flex, bend, and twist easily while carving turns or easing down steep trails. The fleece-lined hood with detachable faux fur edging kept his head and ears warm on icy chairlift rides, and he could easily remove the fur for a sleeker après-ski look. Thanks to the drawcords at the neck, it pulls tight around your face to shut out breezes.

This coat has eight pockets—more than any on the list—including roomy zippered chest pockets that fit slim essentials like a phone or cardholder. Its weight-to-warmth ratio is excellent; after five hours on the snow, Speakman stayed warm without feeling like he was wearing a stiff, overstuffed parka. The fit is generous, allowing space to pile base layers and still keep a clean profile.

Down and synthetic insulation are two of the most common options.

Synthetic insulation is made from polyester fibers, more affordable than down, and handles wet weather better. Popular options include PrimaLoft and Thinsulate, which use a blend of synthetic fibers designed to trap heat while remaining lightweight and breathable.

Down is made from clusters of goose or duck plumage, and is prized for its lightweight warmth. It compresses easily for packing and offers superior heat retention in dry conditions. Some coats even blend down and synthetic fill to combine the benefits of both.

Look for a waterproof shell, sealed seams, and a protective hood to help keep rain and snow from soaking through. Features like adjustable cuffs and storm flaps can also help block out wind and moisture. If you’re dealing with wet, snowy winters, prioritize a fully waterproof design over a water-resistant finish.

A winter coat should leave enough room to layer a sweater or hoodie without feeling bulky or restricting movement. The shoulders should sit comfortably, the sleeves should cover the wrists, and the hem should provide enough coverage for your needs. If you plan to wear it over heavier layers, consider sizing up, but always check the brand’s fit recommendations.

Look for fleece-lined hand pockets to keep your fingers warm and interior pockets to protect your phone, wallet, or AirPods from the cold. Extra details like zippered or hidden pockets add practicality, especially for commuting, travel, or outdoor adventures.

Our fashion team, led by Style and Reviews Director Christian Gollayan, tested more than 40 winter coats in real-world conditions, from freezing city commutes to snowy hikes, ski trips, and travel days spent shuffling between cold-weather airports. If a coat claimed to handle winter, we made sure it proved it. We focused on warmth, durability, fit, mobility, and practicality. We paid attention to how each coat insulated in different temperatures, whether the materials could stand up to wind and wet weather, how well the coat moved with us during long days out, and whether the design felt useful rather than overbuilt.

Details like pocket placement, zippers, adjustability, and overall comfort played a big role too. After months of wear and side-by-side comparisons, only the top performers made our final list. These are the winter coats that stayed warm, held up, and made our lives easier—not just in theory, but in brutal winter reality.

For most of us, the terms "jacket" and "coat" are probably interchangeable. However, the main difference comes down to length and coverage. A winter coat's main objective is to keep you warm, which is why it's bigger and thicker, extends past the hips or toward the knees, and is filled with some type of insulation. A jacket, on the other hand, is considered a combination of style and warmth. Jackets don't typically go past the waist and they're designed to be worn indoors at times. Winter jackets can be layered more with outfits too—sometimes even under a coat.

Winter jackets can work as your main outer layer in cold weather, especially when they’re insulated and long enough to provide adequate coverage. For colder temperatures or extended time outdoors, a longer, more heavily insulated coat or parka can provide additional warmth and protection. The right choice ultimately depends on the weather, your activity level, and how much you plan to layer underneath.

As traditional giants rush into digital dollars, USDD’s Yvonne Chia explains why 24/7 access, self-custody, and transparent yield give decentralized stablecoins an edge banks can’t replicate.

20 November – Road Town, Totorla, British Virgin Islands – Decentralized stablecoin protocol USDD is accelerating its multichain utility across TRON, Ethereum, and BNB Chain—combining automated sUSDD yield via its Smart Allocator with GasFree zero-TRX transfers—as traditional financial giants race to build competing stablecoin rails.

In a recent industry interview with instant exchange partner ChangeNOW, USDD Head of Communications Yvonne Chia outlined why self-custody, 24/7 settlement, and transparent onchain reserves give decentralized digital dollars a structural advantage over bank-issued alternatives.

For billions of people globally, opening and maintaining a traditional bank account still involves paperwork, minimum balance requirements, geographic restrictions, and approval delays. Even when banks integrate stablecoin rails behind the scenes, those services remain gated behind legacy compliance walls and intermediary control.

Crypto-native stablecoins flip that model on its head. As Yvonne Chia highlighted during the interview:

“Compare this to a stablecoin like USDD, where all you need is a phone, a working internet connection, you can immediately start a wallet and you have access to your funds right away.”

With USDD, users can access and manage their digital dollars directly through their own wallets, without depending on traditional financial intermediaries.

This represents a fundamental shift in financial access: users are no longer limited to the services, operating hours, or account structures of a single institution. Instead, they have the freedom to hold, manage, and transfer their assets on their own terms.

Self-custody also gives users greater autonomy over their financial decisions. They can choose which wallets to use, where to transfer their assets, and which supported decentralized applications to interact with, without needing to route every transaction through a centralized financial institution.

With USDD, users’ digital dollars can move with them across an open blockchain ecosystem, rather than remaining tied to a particular bank or service provider.

Legacy payment networks still operate on decades-old schedules: weekend cutoffs, bank holidays, and multi-day cross-border settlement delays accompanied by hefty wire fees.

Blockchain networks never close. Whether it is a Sunday night or a public holiday, USDD moves globally without depending on traditional banking operating hours or settlement windows.

“We are able to have transfers 24/7 and we’re not limited to any traditional banking hours. So I think that in some ways, stablecoins are not just becoming banks, but exceeding what traditional banks can offer to users.”

To make everyday transfers even smoother than fintech apps, USDD introduced GasFree integration on TRON, allowing users on supported wallets to pay network fees directly in USDD without needing to hold TRX.

This removes another practical barrier to stablecoin adoption: having to acquire and maintain a separate gas token just to transfer digital dollars. With GasFree, eligible users can pay approximately 0.5 USDD per transaction, compared with around 1.5 USDT for a standard USDT transfer under the referenced fee conditions.

These improvements matter because the usefulness of a stablecoin is not determined by its peg alone. Low-cost transfers, straightforward wallet experiences, and around-the-clock availability are what make digital dollars practical for everyday payments and global value transfers.

Perhaps the sharpest contrast between banks and decentralized stablecoins lies in how yield is distributed.

In traditional banking, institutions take customer deposits, deploy them into yield-generating markets, and retain a significant portion of the returns. Everyday depositors may receive relatively low interest rates, while higher-yielding products often come with eligibility requirements, minimum deposits, or fixed maturity periods.

Stablecoins introduce another way to participate in digital-dollar opportunities. Rather than keeping capital entirely within a traditional deposit account, users can access onchain yield opportunities through decentralized protocols and transparent investment mechanisms.

USDD was built to return that value directly to holders. Through USDD Earn, users can deposit USDD to receive sUSDD, earning automated, competitive yield powered by our Smart Allocator system, with no fixed lock-up periods restricting access to their capital.

For users, the distinction is important: USDD Earn provides access to a productive stablecoin while maintaining flexibility, rather than requiring users to commit their capital to a conventional fixed-term product.

Traditional banks ask customers to trust closed-door balance sheets and periodic regulatory filings—until a crisis proves otherwise.

USDD takes a different approach through its “Don’t trust, verify” ethos, emphasizing publicly accessible onchain information and independent verification.

Transparency does not eliminate financial or technical risks, but it changes how users can evaluate them. Instead of relying exclusively on an institution’s assurances, users have access to information that can be independently examined and verified.

The bigger picture is an interconnected financial ecosystem in which users can move between holding, transferring, exchanging, and deploying their stablecoins according to their own needs. These are not isolated functions. Together, they make stablecoins more useful as everyday financial infrastructure.

Banks will undoubtedly continue using stablecoin rails to modernize their back-end settlement. However, true financial freedom comes from open networks where assets flow freely across protocols without intermediaries.

For USDD, the opportunity goes beyond offering a dollar-pegged asset. It is about making digital dollars accessible, transferable, and productive across an interconnected financial ecosystem. From self-custody and 24/7 transfers to flexible yield opportunities and multichain DeFi access, these capabilities give users more ways to put their money to work.

Banks may be bringing stablecoins into traditional finance. Crypto-native protocols are showing what stablecoins can make possible beyond it.

The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Three XRP Ledger amendments linked to native lending have each gained two validator votes since Nov. 17, according to XRPScan data. As of Nov. 20, 2026, Single Asset Vault (XLS-65) had 25 votes, and Lending Protocol (XLS-66) and the LendingProtocolV1_1 patch had 24 votes each.

XRPScan data shows that LendingProtocolV1_1 has been up for a vote since Sept. 29, 2026, when it came with the v3.4.0 release. According to the patch's voting history, it had about 19 votes for most of October. It started to gain votes again in late October. XRP was trading at $0.96 on Friday.

Lending is built directly into the XRP Ledger's code, with no third-party smart contracts. According to Ripple, lenders deposit into a Single Asset Vault, and the Lending Protocol lets loan brokers use that capital "to issue loans and track repayments onchain."

The model is close to how banks lend. Loans have fixed terms and a repayment schedule, and credit brokers vet borrowers before the loans are issued. On Nov. 19, Clearpool showed the full lending flow on the XRPL Devnet with Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin. In the demo, "An approved lender funds a private vault, and a borrower accepts and repays a loan underwritten offchain by a broker," Clearpool wrote.

Through Single Asset Vault (XLS-65), XRP holders will be able to deposit their coins into shared liquidity pools, and institutional borrowers will take loans from those pools at a fixed rate. After the loan is repaid, "the lender redeems at a higher share price," according to the Clearpool demo.

The amendments still need more votes before they can activate. "An amendment needs more than 80% support, held for 14 days, to activate," XRPScan says on its amendment pages. For the current set of 35 validators, the site puts the threshold at "more than 80% of 35 votes, so 29 needed."

#5231. Bitcoin institutional holdings hit $29.78B – What changed in Q3?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Things have changed dramatically since the third quarter of 2026, when institutional interest in Bitcoin [BTC] increased. After three quarters of net selling, institutional investors resumed net purchases of spot Bitcoin exchange-traded products (ETPs).

According to Alex Thorn from Galaxy Research, institutions added approximately 49,229 BTC-equivalent during the three-month period.  Notably, by the 30th of September, institutional investment managers held a record 356,491 BTC-equivalent, worth approximately $29.78 billion.

The growing role of financial advisors and wealth management platforms played a major role.

Together, they held 144,307 BTC-equivalent by the end of September, representing 40.5% of all Bitcoin ETP holdings reported by institutional managers. If looked back, their holdings have increased for nine consecutive quarters and are now 3.3 times higher than their March 2024 levels.

That being said, large banks played a major role in this accumulation, with Wells Fargo, Bank of America, and Morgan Stanley being among the biggest buyers during Q3.

Wells Fargo alone added 14,636 BTC-equivalent, taking its total holdings to 30,553 BTC-equivalent, making it the largest institutional holder of U.S. spot Bitcoin ETPs, overtaking Jane Street.

Institutional ownership also shifted, with hedge funds dropping from 50.6% in December 2024 to 19%, while financial advisors and wealth platforms increased their exposure. Of this, BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for 65.2% of institutional Bitcoin ETP holdings.

That said, Bitcoin ETP holdings fell by 38,531 BTC between the 30th of September and the 16th of November.

However, the tokenized ETP sector continued to struggle, with its market capitalization falling 6.2% to $595 million and trading volume declining to $160 million, as previously reported by AMBCrypto.

This comes as Bitcoin spot ETFs recorded net inflows of $2.65 billion in September 2026 and $3.52 billion in August, while July saw smaller inflows of $172.43 million. However, the trend reversed in October, with $515.03 million in net outflows, followed by significantly larger outflows of $3.47 billion in November 2026.

Presently, only 130 crypto whale wallets qualified for Trump’s fancy memecoin dinner at the golf club.

Just 130 crypto wallets secured seats for the November 22 TRUMP token holder dinner at Donald Trump’s Virginia golf club, leaving dozens of the 185 available places unclaimed. The Official Trump token was trading near record lows at the time of the close.

The event is designed to reward the largest holders, with the top 29 wallets also eligible for a VIP reception. Contest participants held roughly $8.6 million in tokens combined when the qualification period ended, a sharp drop in engagement from the project’s first holder dinner.

BREAKING: 🇺🇸 Trump will host an exclusive dinner for the top 185 $TRUMP holders this Sunday.The coin is down 99% from its peak. pic.twitter.com/NxizWHlrVg

Ranking was based on time-weighted holdings, which encouraged accumulation and retention through the window.

More than 5,000 eligible holders reportedly did not register. The leaderboard’s combined value represented only a small fraction of TRUMP’s roughly $268 million market capitalization.

TRUMP was trading around $0.95 in the latest reporting, down roughly 46% over the prior month after setting a record low near $0.896 on November 14. The token remains well below its peak, with one account describing it as down almost 99% from its high.

Large holders added to positions during the dip. Nansen data showed the top 100 wallets increased their combined holdings by 1.27% over 30 days, while a separate whale cohort expanded holdings by 26.63%. Exchange balances fell slightly over the same period.

Top-ranked winners risk losing VIP benefits if balances drop below specified levels before the event, and lower-ranked winners can forfeit their seat by selling more than half their qualifying balance. Those restrictions expire once the dinner is over.

Ahead of the 2025 dinner, 92 of 220 invited holders reportedly sold their entire positions before the event.

A Super Bowl-themed leaderboard planned for February 2027 may give some buyers a reason to stay involved, but it does not remove the immediate question of whether winners will take liquidity afterward.

Dogecoin has shaved about 9% off its futures-to-spot volume ratio over 24 hours, suggesting that risk-off tendencies are taking over investors’ desire to expose themselves to volatility.

Futures quite often precede a pickup in volatility. A reduction in futures positions suggests a way calmer market dynamic, as fewer leveraged positions are there to amplify price moves. Open interest fell 2.25% over the same window. Spot turnover grew faster than futures turnover, which explains why the ratio went down while trading picked up in both markets.

CoinGlass still recorded around $4.4 million in net spot selling. Futures saw around $1.4 million in net buying, even as the total value of open positions declined. The market may be taking some risk off, and spot sellers still have the upper hand. CoinGlass volume and flows

The local decline in volume is unlikely to help the price in the medium to long term, and the possibility of the trend aggravating is still there.

#5227. Michael Saylor prioritizes STRC buybacks as Strategy’s Bitcoin buying slows 90% – Why?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Nothing highlights the impact of ongoing market volatility better than Strategy.

In a recent interview, Michael Saylor outlined a potential shift in Strategy’s approach. He explained why the company could sell MSTR shares even below its net Bitcoin value to buy back STRC. The key takeaway? The market is calling this arguably the most revealing part of the 19th of November’s investor Q&A.

Fundamentally, this seems logical. As outlined below, MSTR has performed extremely poorly as Bitcoin has fallen, losing over 40% of value within Q4. If MSTR loses another 25% of value, it will have lost more this quarter than last year’s Q4 crash, potentially making it the worst quarter MSTR has had since the bear market back in 2022.

The result? Strategy’s Bitcoin [BTC] accumulation has slowed sharply in Q4 2026.

In Q4 2025, Strategy bought 32,470 BTC. In comparison, it has only bought 3,183 BTC so far in Q4 2026. This represents a drop of 90%. To date, Strategy also used $206.3 million proceeds from selling MSTR shares to buy STRC shares. However, only $33.4 million has been used to buy Bitcoin.

In short, broader market weakness is putting Strategy under pressure. Against this backdrop, Michael Saylor’s latest STRC strategy doesn’t look like a random move. Strategy seems to be shifting more capital toward supporting its preferred stock while navigating a difficult market. But with FUD around the company continuing to build, the bigger question is whether STRC can still attract enough investor demand to support Strategy’s Bitcoin accumulation plans.

One thing is clear: Strategy’s main priority is to keep STRC stable.

As one analyst pointed out, this could mean the company would continue selling MSTR shares to fund STRC buybacks. If that isn’t enough, Strategy could also sell Bitcoin whenever STRC trades below its $100 par value. Saylor believes STRC’s 12% dividend is already attractive enough, making it a key income-generating product for institutional investors.

But what does this mean for Strategy shareholders? As the chart below shows, major institutional investors increased their MSTR holdings in Q3 2026. The top 15 now own around 33% of all outstanding shares. This shows that big investors are still interested in MSTR despite market weakness.

However, with Strategy focusing more on STRC, will MSTR shareholders still benefit from its BTC strategy?

Notably, this is where a potential feedback loop comes in. Continued weakness in MSTR could push Strategy to rely more on STRC buybacks to support its capital structure. However, this could also put institutional demand for MSTR at risk. If investor confidence weakens, raising fresh capital for future STRC buybacks could become more difficult.

So, for now, Saylor’s shift towards STRC signals a “risky” change in how Strategy plans to fund future BTC purchases.

Strategy is focusing more on STRC buybacks as MSTR struggles, potentially slowing Bitcoin purchases.

STRC’s 12% dividend may attract investors, but can it maintain demand without hurting MSTR?
